user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

To assist you with the MMS issue, I first need to identify you as a customer. Could you please provide me with your phone number, or your full name along with your date of birth? This will help me look up your account and check your line status and settings.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth, or is that enough?

For name-based lookup, I do need your date of birth for verification. Since you provided your phone number, I can start by looking up your customer information using the phone number. I will proceed with that now.

I have found your account, John Smith. To help resolve the MMS issue, I will first check the status of your phone's cellular service and mobile data, as these are prerequisites for sending MMS. I will also check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions for MMS. I will start by checking the status bar on your phone to see the current network and data status.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I see that my phone shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top of the screen. Does that mean something is wrong with my connection? What should I do next?

Since your phone shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," it means your phone currently has no cellular service and mobile data is turned off. This is why your MMS messages are not going through.

Let's start by checking if Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone, as that would disable all wireless connections including cellular service and data. If Airplane Mode is on, we will turn it off.

Your line is active and not suspended, so the issue is likely with your phone settings. Let's proceed by checking if Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. If it is, I will guide you to turn it off. May I check the Airplane Mode status on your phone now?

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
It looks like Airplane Mode is already turned off on my phone. But I also see something about the SIM card being "missing" and no service. Is that a problem? What should I do about that?

If your phone shows the SIM card as "missing," it means your phone is not detecting the SIM card properly, which would cause no cellular service and no data connection.

The best next step is to try reseating the SIM card. This means removing the SIM card from your phone and then reinserting it carefully to ensure it is properly seated.

Would you like me to guide you through the process of reseating your SIM card?
Oh, that sounds a bit scary—I’m always worried I’ll break something or lose my photos. If I do this, will it mess up anything else on my phone? And is it safe for someone like me to try?

Reseating the SIM card is a safe and simple process that will not affect your photos, apps, or any other data on your phone. The SIM card only stores your carrier information needed for cellular service, so removing and reinserting it will not delete or change anything on your phone.

I can guide you step-by-step to make sure you do it correctly and safely. Would you like me to proceed with the instructions?

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I went ahead and reinserted the SIM card as you suggested. Now, at the top of my screen, I see a signal bar (though it says "Poor") and something about "2G," but it still says "Data Disabled." What should I do next?

Great, the SIM card is now detected, and you have some signal, though it's poor and on 2G. The "Data Disabled" means your mobile data is still turned off, which is why MMS won't work.

Next, please enable mobile data on your phone. This will allow your phone to use the cellular network for internet access, which is required for sending MMS.

Would you like me to guide you on how to turn mobile data on?

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I’ve turned on mobile data. Now the top of my screen says "Data Enabled," but it still shows "2G" and the signal is still poor. Is that going to be a problem for sending picture messages? What should I do next?

The "2G" network is generally not suitable for sending MMS (picture messages) because it is a slower network technology. For MMS to work properly, your phone should connect to at least a 3G or higher network.

I will check your phone's network mode preference and help you change it to a mode that prefers 4G or 5G if needed. Let me check that now.
